content.value_statement: Privacy obligations are complex across regions and data types. This skill guides assessments, request workflows, notices, consent controls, and breach response.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and HIPAA scope, duties, rights, and notification timelines.
Outlines workflows for access, deletion, portability, objection, and consent requests.
Provides examples for consent records, cookie banners, and privacy preference controls.
Explains privacy-by-design practices for minimization, purpose limitation, and retention.
Supplies DPIA, privacy policy, breach response, and compliance checklist templates.
limitations: It is guidance and does not replace qualified legal advice.
Regulatory summaries may need review for current local requirements.
Example workflows must be adapted to each data system and business process.
It does not connect to systems or enforce privacy controls automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Privacy Controls
use_cases.description: Map a new product feature to consent, minimization, retention, and data subject rights requirements before launch.

use_cases.title: Document Compliance Procedures
use_cases.description: Create practical procedures for GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, or HIPAA requests, notices, and breach response activities.

use_cases.title: Review Engineering Designs
use_cases.description: Check whether proposed data flows include lawful basis, access controls, retention limits, and deletion paths.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Applicable Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a product or service
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product description and identify likely GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and HIPAA obligations. Explain the main risks in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Rights Request Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a data subject rights workflow for access, deletion, correction, portability, and objection requests. Include verification, deadlines, records, and exceptions.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a DPIA Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a DPIA for this processing activity. Cover purpose, data types, subjects, recipients, risks, mitigations, retention, and approval steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Cross-Regulation Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and HIPAA requirements for this data flow. Produce shared controls, regulation-specific controls, gaps, and next actions.

output_examples.input: Assess a new analytics feature that tracks page views, account IDs, and marketing campaign source.
output: Likely obligations include notice, consent or opt-out review, retention limits, and purpose documentation.
Recommended controls include minimized identifiers, consent checks before tracking, aggregation, and a deletion path.
Open questions include data sharing with vendors and whether profiling or targeted advertising is involved.

output_examples.input: Create a deletion request procedure for a SaaS application with backups and payment records.
output: Verify identity, locate personal data, and separate data that must be retained for legal obligations.
Delete or anonymize application data, queue backup deletion, revoke credentials, and log the decision.
Send a clear response explaining completed deletion, retained records, legal basis, and retention period.

output_examples.input: Review a privacy policy draft for missing GDPR and CCPA/CPRA disclosures.
output: The review highlights controller identity, data categories, purposes, sharing, rights, retention, transfers, and contact details.
The response flags vague use descriptions and missing opt-out language for sale or sharing.
The final section lists practical edits for counsel and compliance review.

best_practices: Provide the exact data flow, data categories, jurisdictions, and vendors before asking for compliance guidance.
Ask for controls that engineering, legal, and operations teams can each validate.
Have qualified counsel review outputs before publishing policies or making legal decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat sample templates as final legal documents without local review.
Do not collect sensitive data because a template mentions it as an example.
Do not rely on consent alone when another lawful basis or sector rule applies.

faq.question: Can this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides practical guidance and templates, but qualified counsel should review legal positions and notices.

faq.question: Which regulations does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA, and general international privacy principles at a practical level.

faq.question: Can it create data subject request workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline verification, response deadlines, fulfillment steps, exceptions, and audit records.

faq.question: Does it connect to company systems?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and guidance only. It does not access databases, vendors, or production systems.

faq.question: Can it help with breach response planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes breach response timelines, notification considerations, and communication template guidance.

faq.question: How should teams use the generated templates?
faq.answer: Teams should adapt them to actual processing, data retention, vendors, jurisdictions, and internal approval processes.
